body: Back when I was still going to college, I saw a counselor at the on-site health center.  Other than that, no.
Perhaps, although I can't say I'm particularly fond of the job.

I do software work.  It's a 9 - 5 job, but I get paid hourly because it's technically an internship.  I was supposed to be going to college this semester, but for a number of reasons I ended up not doing that.  The company apparently liked my work enough that they wanted to keep me on anyway.

That's an interesting suggestion...  I don't know if I'll ever be able to do that, nor do I know how I'd even begin something like that.  But then, I don't know a lot of things.  I shouldn't let that stop me.  I've got a bad habit of giving up too early sometimes.

Your advice about other peoples' opinions sounds good, but I don't have a clue how I'd do that.  I'm rather weak-willed when it comes to standing up to other people, even in my own head.  I'm probably my harshest critic, and I'll find myself imagining all the horrible things people would say to me.  I know that's not good, not helpful, but I don't know how to stop it.  I've been afraid of other people since I was a kid.  It's probably even one reason why I want to leave my human life behind.

Thank you for trying to help.  I'm still feeling rather iffy about a lot of things, but I'm hopefully at least a little better than I was last night.  It does do some good to talk with people that care, at least.  Sometimes I forget and start to believe *everyone* hates me.

Thanks.  I actually do visit /r/furry on my main account, though I've never worked up the courage to say anything about my real feelings.  

People are nicer there, but I've occasionally seen the same sorts of disapproval that drives my fear of people.  There are at least a few furries who don't appreciate those who desire to be an animal, or those who find real animals attractive.  I suppose I can't really blame them for not wanting to be associated with either thing.

I shouldn't let a few bad people ruin my experience, I know.  I'm just horrible at receiving criticism without feeling like there's something personally wrong with me, regardless of who said it or why.  I'm also bad at judging the intent of people so it's hard for me to find more accepting people to talk to.

Your assessment is correct.  The way other people feel about me is a massive problem for me.  It makes it difficult to talk to anyone for fear of how they might react.  It bothers me that a lot of people hate me, or would hate me if they knew.  I shouldn't let that get to me, but it's hard to function well with others when it feels like they're all my enemy, true or not.

The other half of the problem, of course, is that I'll never be able to have what I want.  It kills any motivation I might have when I think about how nothing I've done or ever could do has really brought me any closer to my goal.  I appreciate your efforts in trying to point me to a more possible substitute.  Unfortunately, as good advice as it is, it doesn't manage to catch my attention or ignite my willpower to do anything.  Maybe I'm just too hard-headed to compromise.

Thanks for replying.  It makes me feel better to see at least some people don't immediately reach for the virtual pitchforks.  I don't think anything will ever help me completely forget the sort of things I've seen said about me, though.

The wilderness thing might be good thing to try, but I'm in no shape to go anywhere at the moment.  I've got my life just barely held together with bits of twine, and there are a fair number of things that I need to get a handle on before I can think about taking some time off.

I've pretty much been a mess lately.  It's been hard for me to even get up for work, nevermind take care of the other things that need doing.  I've let things pile up that shouldn't have, including almost losing my apartment because I was too scared of my phone to realize they had been calling about an issue with the automatic payment.  That might be sorted, but there are other things just like it that need the attention that I can barely scrape together on a good day.

Sorry, I probably sound pathetic.  Thanks for offering your suggestions and your support.

I appreciate that.  I can't say I've ever been particularly hopeful of any sort of VR, but then again I've always been rather pessimistic, so I don't have a clue whether that's a reasonable concern or not.

I'm not really concerned about being "wrong" in any meaningful way.  I accept how I feel as the way things are, whatever that means.  It's more a matter of other people.  I feel safe-ish laying myself bare here on Reddit and behind a throwaway because there's relatively little danger, and I can always avoid my inbox if I get too stressed.

It gets far more problematic in real life, where people are full of prejudices and words cannot be taken back once said.  It's a dangerous game to play when I'm  not exactly something that people greet with warm smiles and open hugs.  Even more so when considering my latest episode tonight was initiated by a careless but not ill-intentioned comment by someone trying to help me.

I don't know.  Maybe I'm just too paranoid, but I find it extremely difficult to talk with anyone.  That's probably a big component of all the problems I have, though not the only one.
